headline: Genk favourites at home, but Standard still create chances
summary: Standard Liege arrive at the Cegeka Arena on three straight league defeats — 0-1 at home to Charleroi, 1-2 at Gent, 2-4 at Westerlo. Genk's last league game at home was a 3-0 win over Kortrijk. But Standard create more: 1.81 expected goals a game against Genk's 1.27, and they won on their last visit here in February. Belgian outlets report Casper Nielsen could miss out with a foot injury. Across 10 bookmakers, margin removed, Genk are 54.2% favourites and rated 0.71 goals better; over 3.0 goals is 49.7%.
read: Genk are clear home favourites at 54.2%, rated about three-quarters of a goal better than a Standard side that has lost its last three league games. Standard do create chances — 1.81 xG per game — and won 3-0 on their last visit to Genk, but the market sees the goals at 3.0 with both teams to score at 59.5%.

facts.fact: Genk are clear favourites at 54.2% to win, more than two and a half times Standard Liege's 20.1%.
facts.meaning: The market expects the home side to take the three points, with Standard given roughly a one-in-five chance.

facts.fact: Standard have lost their last three league matches — 0-1 at home to Charleroi, 1-2 at Gent and 2-4 at Westerlo.
facts.meaning: The visitors come in on a losing league run, with only the midweek cup win over Dender interrupting it.

facts.fact: The market rates Genk about three-quarters of a goal better, with the Asian handicap fair line at -0.71.
facts.meaning: A single-goal Genk win is roughly the expected margin — the market does not see a rout.

facts.fact: Standard midfielder Casper Nielsen is uncertain for Sunday after a foot injury at Dender, with Belgian outlets reporting he could miss the trip to Genk.
facts.meaning: Standard could lose one of their regular midfielders for a game where they will spend long spells without the ball.

facts.fact: Genk won their last home league match 3-0 against Kortrijk on 10 October.
facts.meaning: The Cegeka Arena has already produced a convincing home performance from Genk this season.

facts.fact: Standard average 1.81 xG per game over their last five, more than Genk's 1.27.
facts.meaning: The underdog creates chances like the stronger side — the gap in the price is about results, not chance quality.

facts.fact: The goals market sits at 3.0, with Over priced at 49.7% — a coin flip on three goals or more.
facts.meaning: An open game is expected: the market does not lean towards a tight 1-0 or a shootout.

facts.fact: Both teams to score is priced at 59.5% — more likely than not.
facts.meaning: The market leans towards both sides finding the net at the Cegeka Arena.

sources.fact: Casper Nielsen is uncertain for Standard's trip to Genk after a Dender defender stepped on his foot, which swelled up; Belgian outlets report he could miss the match.
Standard could be forced to do without midfielder Casper Nielsen for Sunday's league trip to Genk due to his foot injury.
Standard beat Dender 2-0 in the Belgian Cup to reach the round of 16, though Belgian media described the performance as unconvincing.
Belgian media reported that Standard's cup win over Dender was far from reassuring and raised psychological questions around the team.
Dimitri Lavalée played his first minutes of the season with Standard's first team against Dender after a long spell out.
Genk have organised a special return to the Cegeka Arena for Mike Origi and his son Divock Origi around Sunday's home match against Standard.
A recently retired former Red Devil will give the kick-off for Genk-Standard on Sunday, with Mike and Divock Origi returning to the Cegeka Arena.
